Package io.mavlink4j.testkit

Class DirectTxScheduler

java.lang.Object
io.mavlink4j.testkit.DirectTxScheduler
All Implemented Interfaces:
TxScheduler, AutoCloseable
public final class DirectTxScheduler extends Object implements TxScheduler
A TxScheduler with no threads and no timers: submit(java.lang.String, java.lang.Runnable) runs inline and a repeat(java.lang.String, java.time.Duration, java.lang.Runnable) registration only fires when the test calls tick(). Lets a streaming service (heartbeat, manual control) be driven tick by tick, deterministically.

  • Method Details

    • repeat

      public TxScheduler.Handle repeat(String name, Duration period, Runnable task)
      Description copied from interface: TxScheduler
      Runs task every period, starting immediately, until the returned TxScheduler.Handle is closed. A task that throws is logged and the schedule continues — one bad periodic task must never silently stop firing without a trace, and must never take down another task sharing the same scheduler.
      Specified by:
      repeat in interface TxScheduler
      Parameters:
      name - used only for diagnostics (thread naming, log messages) — not an identity key

    • submit

      public void submit(String name, Runnable task)
      Description copied from interface: TxScheduler
      Runs task once, as soon as a pool thread is free — the latency-sensitive counterpart to TxScheduler.repeat(java.lang.String, java.time.Duration, java.lang.Runnable) for a TX path that must not wait for the next tick of a periodic task (a stick that moves 1 ms after a tick should not pay a full period for a clock that had no reason to be where it was). Same catch-and-log contract as TxScheduler.repeat(java.lang.String, java.time.Duration, java.lang.Runnable) — a task that throws is logged and never reaches the pool — and the same "already shut down" tolerance: a submission racing scheduler shutdown is dropped, not thrown, since callers submit from threads that must not fail on teardown.

      No TxScheduler.Handle is returned: a one-shot that has already been handed to the pool cannot usefully be cancelled, and every caller re-checks its own state when the task actually runs.

      Specified by:
      submit in interface TxScheduler
      Parameters:
      name - used only for diagnostics (log messages) — not an identity key

    • tick
